findings.message: The rewritten Records text says `build_daemon_core` calls `build_control(checkout)` once per core and places that result on the checkout its `bind` closure snapshots. The same text says `build_daemon_core` refuses an absent consumer, and test_production_shares_one_admission_control_consumer must prove that refusal. The test text also requires `CoreRig` to stay unchanged and read `rig.core.control`. `CoreRig` (tests/test_daemon_composition.py:86-100) passes a positional `Checkout` without `control` to `build_daemon_core`. If `build_daemon_core` builds the consumer itself, it can never see an absent one, so the refusal cannot be tested. If it instead refuses a checkout whose `control` is None, the unchanged `CoreRig` is refused and every core-rig test breaks. The spec never says what 'absent' means for `build_daemon_core`: a None `checkout.control` on input, or something else. It also never says whether `build_daemon_core` constructs the consumer or requires the caller to supply it.
findings.paved_road: Harden 19.P3.admission-holds-activation to pick one rule. Option 1: `build_daemon_core` constructs the consumer with `build_control` and puts it on its local checkout; drop it from the absent-consumer refusal list and its test obligation. Option 2: `build_daemon_core` requires a caller-supplied `checkout.control` and refuses None; then fence the `CoreRig` migration and stop calling it unchanged. Regenerate the ticket from the hardened unit.
